title: Questions for you
summary: Every question Claude has asked you, newest first; the list starts on the open ones. You answer in Claude Code; Claude saves your words and updates the plan.

items.question: Benchmark settings: vendor defaults, matched settings, or both?
items.why_it_matters: A duplicate: please answer [the question on browser settings](ref:Q-117) instead.

items.question: Chrome build for benchmarks: normal Chrome with updates blocked, or Chrome for Testing?
items.why_it_matters: A duplicate: please answer [the question on which Chrome to use](ref:Q-118) instead.

items.question: WebView2 runtime for benchmarks: self-updating, fixed version, or both?
items.why_it_matters: A duplicate: please answer [the question on which WebView2 version to use](ref:Q-119) instead.

items.question: Claude renamed its end-of-session notes so each file name starts with the note's id, as the wiki rules require. Keep the new names?
items.why_it_matters: Nothing changes for you. Saying yes, or approving the rule book in the first wave, closes this.
items.answer: Yes: keep the new file names.

items.question: Do you confirm the proposed non-goals (no extensions, no sync or accounts, Windows 11 only, not a full browser) and moving split view to after P8?
items.why_it_matters: These are not in your brief, so they need your word. They fix the scope; asked in the first wave, before P0 ends.
items.answer: Yes, for now: all the non-goals and moving split view to after the last phase. You may add bookmarks once the planned work is done.

items.question: May the plan app write approval entries into the wiki log?
items.why_it_matters: Decides who keeps the log of approvals.
items.answer: Yes. Later replaced: approvals are now given in Claude Code and recorded by Claude.

items.question: Should the plan app offer a 'reset to pending' button for approvals?
items.why_it_matters: It would need a rule-book change, because approval history only grows.

items.question: Keep the accessibility checker (axe-core) that Claude added to the portal's tests on 9 Oct, or remove it?
items.why_it_matters: This question promised to ask you first, but Claude added the checker before you answered. It checks every tab for problems such as poor contrast, popups you cannot close with Esc, and missing labels.
items.answer: Keep it. You first asked what it does and why; Claude explained it checks contrast, popups, labels and page structure, only in tests, at small cost, but cannot judge wording. You said: "Okay, lets add."

items.question: When is the plan app built?
items.why_it_matters: Everything else waits for your approval in it.
items.answer: First, in P0. Your words: 'First the interactive plan comes together. I then approve everything else.'

items.question: Which Node.js version should the plan app use?
items.why_it_matters: The plan app needs Node; changing the main version later can break it.
items.answer: Stay on Node 24 for now; consider 26 later through its own decision. Node 24.20.0 is installed.

items.question: Should the plan app use diagram library Mermaid 12 or the older 11.17.2?
items.why_it_matters: Version 12 was a brand-new, breaking release; 11 was the mature one.
items.answer: Mermaid 12, pinned exactly; fall back to 11.17.2 if drawing breaks.

items.question: May Claude make local git commits, starting in P0?
items.why_it_matters: Without commits, recovering from an interruption cannot rely on git history.
items.answer: Yes, from P0: one local commit per checked task; never upload (push).

items.question: What name, visibility and timing do you want for the GitHub repository?
items.why_it_matters: Automatic checks on GitHub cannot run until it exists. Needed only for the P1 review.

items.question: Do you approve the repository layout: the repo root is the project root, one Rust workspace, plus the extra folders other areas proposed?
items.why_it_matters: P1 creates the project skeleton from this layout, so P1 cannot start without it.
items.answer: Yes: the layout as proposed, with the throwaway test builds kept as evidence.

items.question: How should Ferrum give each website its own WebView2 profile, given that Tauri cannot pass a profile name through yet?
items.why_it_matters: Per-site profiles are central to isolation. Recommended: wait for Tauri, else patch it; direct WebView2 calls only as a last resort. A P1 test informs it; P3 waits on it.

items.question: Should the end-of-phase review with you apply to every phase, including P0 and P1, not only the milestone phases?
items.why_it_matters: Decides whether you formally review P0 and P1 before the next phase starts. Your 10 Oct rule already makes Claude pause after P0 and wait for your go; this asks about the formal review. Asked in the first wave, before P0 ends.
items.answer: Yes: the end-of-phase review with you applies to every phase, planning included.

items.question: How should Ferrum hand Google sign-in over to your normal browser, since Google blocks sign-in inside embedded web views?
items.why_it_matters: A P2 task builds the sign-in detection, so P2 needs the expected behaviour.

items.question: Do you approve one deliberate, audited module that talks to WebView2 directly using unsafe Rust code?
items.why_it_matters: Several needed features are reachable only this way. The decision is part of P1 and P2, so both wait on it.
items.answer: Yes: one carefully reviewed module for the direct WebView2 calls.

items.question: Should a 'site' mean the registrable domain, the exact origin, or containers you define?
items.why_it_matters: Sets how finely websites are kept apart. P3 builds per-site settings on it.

items.question: What exactly should happen with http: addresses: upgrade to HTTPS, and what if the upgrade fails?
items.why_it_matters: P4 sets the final web address rules; P2 ships a simple interim version.

items.question: What should the default blocklist contain, and where should it come from?
items.why_it_matters: P4 builds the security policy engine that uses it.

items.question: Where should the network log live, how long is it kept, and should the query part of web addresses (which can hold tokens) be removed by default?
items.why_it_matters: Privacy of the local network log. P5 builds it. Recommended: remove query strings by default.

items.question: May 'time to interactive' be replaced by first-paint and largest-paint timings plus long-frame data, since that measure is retired?
items.why_it_matters: Your brief asks for it, but it is now considered unreliable. P5 builds the startup timing.

items.question: What is the exact CPU model and RAM of the benchmark machine?
items.why_it_matters: The CPU generation decides which energy counters work. The energy experiment in P6 waits on it.

items.question: Should benchmarks compare the browsers as shipped, with matched settings, or both?
items.why_it_matters: Chrome and Edge have power-saving features on by default. The framing must be fixed before any data. Recommended: both, with as-shipped as the headline.

items.question: Should benchmarks use normal Chrome (updates paused) or the special Chrome for Testing build?
items.why_it_matters: Normal Chrome is what people use; the test build is easier to repeat. Recommended: normal Chrome and Edge, versions recorded.

items.question: Should benchmarks use the self-updating WebView2 runtime, a fixed version, or both?
items.why_it_matters: Affects how repeatable results are. Recommended: self-updating for the headline results, fixed version as a separate setup.

items.question: Which public websites should the extra real-world tests use?
items.why_it_matters: Recommended: Claude proposes a shortlist in P6 and you pick 5 to 8, no logins. Their results stay separate from local test pages.

items.question: Which Python environment tool should the analysis use?
items.why_it_matters: Fixes how others can rerun the analysis. Proposed: a standard virtual environment with exact versions.

items.question: Do you have a wall-power meter?
items.why_it_matters: Without one, energy is only estimated from CPU counters or marked unsupported. The energy experiment waits on it.

items.question: Do you approve installing the PawnIO kernel driver and running an energy sampler with admin rights?
items.why_it_matters: Needed for CPU energy readings. No kernel driver is installed without your approval.

items.question: Which venue should the paper target?
items.why_it_matters: Not needed until results exist. The paper phase waits on it.

items.question: The look you chose puts the tabs in the window's top bar. Should the first version keep the normal Windows title bar above the tabs until that is checked?
items.why_it_matters: Tabs in the top bar need a custom title bar, which has a known resize problem in Tauri; not checked yet (checked in P1). Claude suggests the normal title bar first. Needed before tabs are built (P3).

items.question: Do you approve the proposed 'meaningful difference' thresholds and the weights of the combined score?
items.why_it_matters: Both must be fixed before data is collected in P6 and before the tab-sleeping settings are frozen in P7.

items.question: For local test pages: install a local development certificate (HTTPS), allow plain HTTP on this PC for tests only, or use public HTTPS sites?
items.why_it_matters: Every option touches security. The P2 test server needs it, and P4 sets the final web address rules around it. Recommended: local certificate plus a few public HTTPS sites.

items.question: Where should raw benchmark data be stored, and how should very large files be handled?
items.why_it_matters: P5 is the first phase that can produce run data. Large files may need to live outside git, with only their fingerprints kept.

items.question: Should all main experiments run in one campaign with fixed versions, or each in the phase that builds it?
items.why_it_matters: Affects how comparable the results are, and the schedule.

items.question: Will you accept 10 trials per setup for the long reliability test instead of 30?
items.why_it_matters: Each run is planned at about 2 hours (an estimate, not measured). Fewer trials would be a recorded change from your brief.

items.question: Should the two related-work sections in your paper outline be merged into one?
items.why_it_matters: Your brief lists both. Settles the paper outline.

items.question: The rule book lets a few summary pages stay in the research and risks folders instead of moving them. Keep that rule?
items.why_it_matters: Nothing changes for you: no page moves. Approving the rule book in the first wave keeps the rule and closes this; saying no means Claude moves those pages.
items.answer: Yes: keep the rule. The summary pages stay where they are.

items.question: Should Ferrum with smart tab sleeping be re-run through the other main experiments in P7, or reported only in its own experiment?
items.why_it_matters: Your brief compares it with every other setup. Recommended: re-run, if time allows.

items.question: When a tab moves to another site, should Ferrum move it to that site's profile (losing back/forward history), keep the old profile, or block it?
items.why_it_matters: A trade-off between isolation and convenience; it matters only if per-site profiles are used. Recommended: move it and tell the user.

items.question: May the plan app's tests use a coverage tool and download a test browser?
items.why_it_matters: The full test gate needs both.

items.question: May unsafe code also live in two Windows helper modules for process measurement, each with its own safety notes, or should it all go in one Windows module?
items.why_it_matters: Measurement needs low-level Windows calls. This extends the unsafe-code decision that P1 and P2 wait on. Recommended: two extra modules.
items.answer: Two small extra modules: one for measuring, one in the benchmark robot, each with its own safety notes.

items.question: Is it OK to switch security, isolation and tab-sleeping options at run time on one identical program, with two build-time exceptions?
items.why_it_matters: Your brief asks for 'feature flags'; this is Claude's reading of it. It shapes how P4 and P7 are built and benchmarked.

items.question: Should there be an extra baseline app with a shell plus one web view?
items.why_it_matters: It separates the cost of Ferrum's shell from the cost of Ferrum's own logic. Recommended: yes, as a labelled extra setup.

items.question: Should Ferrum's settings file use the TOML or the JSON format (two common text formats for settings)?
items.why_it_matters: P2 creates the settings file. Recommended: TOML.

items.question: Is a second machine available for a repeat run?
items.why_it_matters: Without one, the paper states the single-machine limit. Nothing waits on it.

items.question: Should the backup wiki check scripts be committed in the tools folder?
items.why_it_matters: They are the backup check when the app cannot run.
items.answer: Yes, commit them under tools. The app's checker stays the main one; the Python scripts are a backup that needs no Node.

items.question: Research predictions and measurements are labelled 'hyp' and 'metric' instead of the 'h' and 'm' of your brief, to fit the wiki's naming rules. Keep that?
items.why_it_matters: Only the labels differ; nothing else changes for you. It needs an answer only before the paper review at the end (P8).

items.question: Who runs tool installs, now that you said 'feel free to run install'?
items.why_it_matters: It contradicted an older rule that you run installs. P1 installs Rust and the C++ build tools.
items.answer: Claude runs all tool installs, including the C++ build tools; you click the admin prompts. Kernel drivers still need your separate approval.

items.question: How should the index list evidence files whose names have capital letters?
items.why_it_matters: The index rule rejected those names, so the wiki check failed and the build paused.
items.answer: List folders, not files. This also scales to benchmark results later.

items.question: May a page's sources be any wiki file or web link?
items.why_it_matters: Four pages failed the new wiki reader's check, which stopped the build.
items.answer: Yes: you accepted all proposed fixes. Any wiki file or https link is allowed; missing targets are flagged; raw research notes are exempt.

items.question: May Claude rewrite the local git history before the first upload to GitHub, so no old commit holds real IP addresses or your user-folder path?
items.why_it_matters: Old commits still hold the values masked on 9 Oct. A rewrite changes every commit id, so it must happen before any upload. It holds the first upload only.
